content:
The image shows a soybean leaf held up for inspection. Key visual features:

- Multiple small, circular to slightly irregular lesions scattered across the leaf surface
- Lesions have a gray/light brown center with distinct reddish-brown to dark brown borders/margins
- Lesions are relatively uniform in size, roughly 3-8mm
- The surrounding leaf tissue remains green with no significant yellowing or chlorosis
- Lesions are on the upper leaf surface and appear to be on both surfaces
- No water-soaking, no pustules, no fungal growth visible

This pattern — gray centers with reddish-brown margins, circular lesions, scattered distribution — is classic Frogeye leaf spot (*Cercospora sojina*). The key diagnostic features match: small circular lesions with gray centers and distinct reddish-purple/brown margins. Septoria brown spot lesions tend to be more irregular and darker brown without the gray center. Phyllosticta lesions are tan/brownish with purplish margins but more irregular.
